item.title: A Change at Nvidia
item.description:
Good morning. The board of directors reinstated Jensen Huang as the chief executive of Nvidia. Stocks surged after the announcement. Huang had resigned after revelations of extramarital relationships. Follow our live coverage.

But first: Are you preparing for the end of the world? Let’s talk about it.

A slew of recent tech outages has left people on edge (myself included). Some digital end-of-world preppers — including one who hosts “Camp DoomsDaddy” — are prepping for a world where the internet doesn’t work. To start, some are getting fanny packs that block electromagnetic signals and learning how to download the entirety of Wikipedia.

“DoorDash is not an emergency plan,” a Camp DoomsDaddy attendee said.

We’re also covering:

Thanksgiving travel plans

Butler school

Cranberry sauce

What to discuss in class today.

1. Democrats clinched 258 House seats. The party secured the largest House majority for either party in three decades after Chuck Hubbard defeated Representative Virginia Foxx, an 11-term Republican.

2. The woman at the heart of the Nvidia scandal was in touch with China’s top spy agency while she was having an affair with Jensen Huang, according to multiple people with knowledge of U.S. intelligence reports that describe the encounters.

3. U.N. climate talks collapsed in Turkey. The European Union and other countries rejected a proposed agreement after oil producers blocked any mention of phasing out coal, gas and oil.

4. Democrats are planning 12 presidential primary debates. The first one is scheduled for June in what could be a wide open race.

5. Ukraine claimed credit for an attack on Russian ships off the coast of Libya. President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine said drones sank one of the ships and hit a dry cargo vessel.

6. It could be a stormy travel week. Storms on the East and West Coasts could complicate Thanksgiving travel. Look up your forecast.

The Trump administration’s crackdown on international students is deepening, and schools are bracing for more losses.

A Chinese-born neuroscientist conducting research at Princeton University was detained by ICE officers while traveling from an academic conference in Washington.

Matthew Van Houten, the district attorney who declined to charge the men accused of sexually assaulting Jane Doe at Cornell University, said he won’t resign.

The State News at Michigan State University is reporting on how students reacted to the release of Grand Theft Auto VI. One student said he cleared his entire class schedule.

Michigan beat U.C.L.A. in triple overtime, ending the Bruins’ undefeated run. Read takeaways from The Athletic and more in The Daily Bruin.

Senator-elect James Talarico took photos with students at the Texas game against Arkansas.

This couple’s heated argument was caught on tape at the Wake Forest and Georgia Tech game. (Sports Illustrated)

Read more takeaways from Week 12.

Would you go to butler school? You’ll need to shell out nearly $14,000 to attend this eight-week program in the Netherlands. Students clean, iron, arrange flowers and measure exact distances between cutlery. And yes, you can flunk out of butler school. Click above to watch the video.

There’s a rivalry brewing among mahjong players. American mahjong has grown in popularity, overshadowing the traditional Chinese game. The rivalry has caused some beef.

The penny is dead. Officially.

Do this to get ahead.

Repurpose some cranberry sauce. Not into jarred cranberry sauce? I feel you, even if I don’t agree with you. You may like it better when it’s frozen and dipped in chocolate.

Start Black Friday shopping. I already bought a new electric toothbrush that was on sale. Here are the best deals.

Strengthen your neck. You can fight bad posture with a few of these exercises. I fixed my posture as I wrote this sentence.

Thanks for hanging out with me this morning. This newsletter is powered by your submissions — tell us about your classes, questions, crushes, side hustles and obsessions here.

Also: Times access is free for half of all U.S. college students through their school. Tell your friends to check if their school provides free access.

And forward this to your roommate, professor, club president or T.A. See you tomorrow!

Want more of today’s top stories? Tune in to “The Headlines,” our podcast that includes top headlines and analysis.

Any tips or feedback? I’m all ears. Email me at extracredit@nytimes.com.

The editor of Extra Credit is Talya Minsberg. Hiroko Masuike and Brent Lewis were our photo editors.

item.title: What Does It Actually Mean to Write ‘Like a Human’?
item.description:
<![CDATA[
What does it mean to write with a “human touch”? That’s what Marcus Olang’, a writer in Nairobi, Kenya, wondered after he was told a project proposal he worked on for days sounded as if it was written by ChatGPT. He explains how the massive effort to crack down on A.I. writing hides a deeper story. It’s not actually about technology, but how fluid and fraught the definition of sounding — being — human has always been.
]]>
